notes.claim: Drawing a square on each side of a right-angled triangle, the largest square has the sum of the areas of the other two (a 3-4-5 triangle gives 25 = 9 + 16).
In any right-angled triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
The hypotenuse is the longest side and is always opposite the right angle.
Finding the hypotenuse means adding the two squares and then taking the square root.
Pythagoras' theorem is only true for right-angled triangles, so it can also check whether a triangle is right-angled.
The area of a square is the side times itself, and pieces of the two small squares can be moved into the hypotenuse square.
